correctness.rationale: The source PGF is normalized at one and factorizes as G(0)(1-rz)/(1-qz)^alpha, with 0<r<q<1. The absolutely summable jump coefficients (alpha q^k-r^k)/k are strictly positive. For each thinning t the unique innovation PGF is H_t(z)=G(z)/G(1-t+tz), with analytic jump coefficients [alpha(q^k-q_t^k)-(r^k-r_t^k)]/k. The ratio of derivatives r_s^{k-1}r_s'/[q_s^{k-1}q_s'] is strictly below A(theta)=r(1-r)/[q(1-q)] for every s<1 and integer k>=1, giving all-parameter sufficiency including equality. When alpha<A(theta), the first logarithmic innovation coefficient is negative for some t sufficiently close to one; thus H_t'(0)<0, proving necessity. The exact identity A(theta)-1=(1-theta-theta^2)/[theta(theta+2)^2] supplies the golden-ratio branch. The rational overlapping WNBL witness gives nu_1(1/2)=-249361/2400900 and was checked in exact arithmetic; finite checks are secondary to the analytic proof.

evidence: Bakouch (2018), pp. 2631-2632, states universal self-decomposability for WNBL and gives PGF (1-p)^(beta+1)(1+p(beta^2-1)z)/[(1+p(beta^2-1))(1-pz)^(beta+1)].
For p=49/51,beta=7/10 this is the PGL law alpha=17/10,theta=2/49, whose thinning quotient at t=1/2 has first logarithmic coefficient -249361/2400900; H_t'(0)<0, ruling out a PGF.
Vardaki and Papageorgiou, REVSTAT in-press manuscript, section 2 and propositions 2.1-2.2, derive PGL convolutions but no all-thinning criterion or stationary-marginal boundary.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The WNBL family is not treated as unrelated; its PGF overlaps the PGL family along a parameter curve, and the published blanket assertion is therefore directly compared. The exact rational negative-coefficient witness disproves implication of that assertion at the overlap; it is not valid stronger coverage. The unrelated 2021 Altun Poisson-generalized Lindley nomenclature is not the same PGF. General closure of negative-binomial convolutions does not supply the sharp PGL necessity.

evidence: Steutel and van Harn establishes a general equivalence, but no model-specific bound.

The Irshad and Rasheed INAR setups use the PGL distribution as the *error* law. Self-decomposability instead decides when it may be the stationary distribution, which is a different inversion problem.

Bakouch gives an overlapping explicit PGF and a universal claim; at a shared rational member its alleged innovation has a negative coefficient and is not a law. This does not subsume the proved classification.
Vardaki and Papageorgiou discuss the relation to Poisson-Lindley plus negative binomial for alpha>2, but addition need not preserve or characterize inverse thinning in both directions.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Each closest assertion was checked for actual implication. Existing PGFs and general criteria may permit derivation of the result, but do not logically assert the evaluated sharp boundary without the sign comparison; a defective blanket assertion does not furnish an equivalent correct proof. The overlap counterexample and all-parameter positivity argument are substantive beyond title/notation differences.

originality.rationale: The new assertion is the sharp family-specific if-and-only-if thinning marginal phase boundary, exact independent innovations for all thinning rates, and a rational counterexample to a published broader self-decomposability assertion on an overlapping count family. Existing papers give the PGL generating function, INAR constructions with PGL *innovations*, a general canonical-sequence criterion, or an unsupported blanket WNBL assertion. The 2018 assertion is inconsistent with a negative first PGF coefficient at an explicitly identical member and cannot mathematically imply the sharp classification. Relevant accessible full material was inspected where available. Priority is best-knowledge, not certified.
residual_risks: Historical priority is not certified: unindexed/unpublished sources could independently contain the exact boundary.

The in-press REVSTAT page image was unavailable, although parsed source text and key sections were accessible.
The WNBL overlap counterexample contradicts its broad published self-decomposability claim; this observation does not assess unrelated WNBL assertions.

value.rationale: For a count distribution already used to drive INAR error processes, the exact condition to use the same family as an invariant marginal is a distinct natural model feasibility problem. The result gives a sharp full-parameter region, closed independent compound-Poisson innovation jump laws for every thinning rate, and a concrete counterexample to an earlier broad statement on an overlapping law. It separates infinite divisibility from thinning self-decomposability, with a golden-ratio threshold controlling universal admissibility. This is a structural complete classification, not an arbitrary single parameter computation or routine table lookup.
